stories.title: US economy grows just 1.5% in Q2, badly missing forecasts as the AI investment boom masks a consumer slowdown
stories.what_happened: The BEA's advance estimate showed the US economy expanded at an annualized **1.5%** rate in Q2 2026 (April–June), missing the 2.1% consensus forecast and decelerating from Q1's 2.1% pace. The composition was unusual: **consumer spending actually picked up sharply**, rising 3.2% versus just 0.5% in the prior quarter, showing households kept spending despite the slowdown. **Business investment excluding housing rose 8.4%**, still strong but down from 10.6% in Q1, and officials pointed to continued heavy investment in AI infrastructure as a key driver. The drag came from **falling government spending** and rising imports, which are subtracted from GDP because they represent money spent on goods produced elsewhere.
key_points: US **GDP** (the total value of everything the economy produced) grew at an annualized **1.5%** in Q2 2026, well below the **2.1%** economists expected.
It's a sharp slowdown from Q1's **2.1%** growth rate.
Consumer spending, which is **~70% of the US economy**, actually accelerated to **3.2%** growth from just 0.5% in Q1.
Business investment outside housing rose **8.4%**, driven largely by a **surge in AI-related spending**.
Government spending fell, and rising imports (which subtract from GDP) also dragged the headline number down.

depth.background: **GDP (Gross Domestic Product)** is the broadest scorecard for an economy — the total dollar value of all goods and services produced in a period. The **Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA)** publishes an early "advance estimate" for each quarter, which markets treat as a key signal of economic health because it feeds directly into decisions the **Federal Reserve** makes about interest rates. Heading into this report, investors were already nervous about tariff costs, a cooling labor market, and whether the massive wave of **AI infrastructure spending** by Big Tech was propping up growth that would otherwise be much weaker.

stories.title: England captain Nat Sciver-Brunt targets a return to bowling — but may sit out the Ireland ODIs
stories.what_happened: Nat Sciver-Brunt said in comments published July 30, 2026 that she is determined to return to bowling as soon as her recovery allows, stating 'I don't want to give up the bowling just yet,' after sustaining a **calf injury** during The Hundred earlier this month. She confirmed she is currently focused on rehabilitation and that her return is being carefully staged by England's medical and performance staff specifically to avoid the injury recurring. Sciver-Brunt has **hinted she could miss England's ODI series against Ireland next month** in order to prioritise a full recovery over rushing back for a lower-stakes series, with her sights instead set on being fully fit for bigger assignments later in the international calendar.
key_points: Sciver-Brunt says she **doesn't want to give up bowling** despite a recurring calf injury, targeting an all-rounder comeback.
She suffered the injury during **The Hundred**, England's domestic short-format tournament, earlier this month.
She has **hinted she may miss** England's ODI series against Ireland next month to protect her recovery.
Her rehab is being **carefully managed** by England's medical and performance staff to avoid a repeat injury.
As **England Women's captain**, her fitness directly affects the team's balance ahead of a busy international calendar.

depth.background: **Nat Sciver-Brunt** is England Women's captain and one of the team's most important all-rounders, meaning she contributes as both a top-order batter and a bowler, giving England extra tactical flexibility. Losing her bowling contribution, even temporarily, forces England to rebalance its bowling attack and batting order. She picked up a calf injury — a strain in the lower leg muscle — while playing in **The Hundred**, England's short, fast domestic cricket competition that runs through the English summer.

stories.title: Supreme Court won't ban pellet guns outright, but orders Delhi to treat protesters injured by them
stories.what_happened: A Supreme Court bench, with Justice Bagchi delivering key remarks, held on Thursday that pellet guns cannot be subject to a **blanket prohibition** because an existing police advisory permits their use in exceptional crowd-control circumstances, and that advisory itself hasn't been legally challenged. The Court said allegations of specific misuse in individual incidents can still be examined **case by case**. At the same time, it **directed the Delhi government to ensure proper medical treatment** for people injured, allegedly by pellet guns, during the protests. It also sought the **Centre's Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)** on pellet gun use and issued formal notice on the broader petition. The plea was brought by **Yashovardhan Azad**, a former Central Information Commissioner and retired IPS officer, along with two individuals who say they were injured, seeking a complete ban on metallic pellet guns for law-and-order use. The underlying incident was the violence during the July 20 Chalo Sansad march over the alleged NEET-UG paper leak.
key_points: The Supreme Court said pellet guns **can't be banned outright** as long as an existing government advisory allows their use for crowd control in exceptional situations.
The Court directed the **Delhi government to ensure proper medical treatment** for people allegedly injured by pellet guns during recent student protests.
The case stems from the **July 20 'Chalo Sansad' march**, where student protesters and police clashed near Jantar Mantar over an alleged **NEET-UG paper leak**.
Petitioners included a **former Central Information Commissioner and retired IPS officer**, plus two people who say they were injured by pellets.
The Court left the door open for **case-by-case scrutiny** of specific alleged misuse, even while declining a blanket ban.

depth.background: Pellet guns fire clusters of small metal or rubber pellets and are officially classed as a 'less lethal' crowd-control weapon, but they've caused serious injuries — including blindings — in India before, most notably during unrest in Jammu & Kashmir. On **July 20, 2026**, a student march called 'Chalo Sansad' (loosely, 'let's go to Parliament') turned violent near Jantar Mantar in Delhi, with protesters angry over an alleged leak of the NEET-UG medical entrance exam paper; clashes broke out between demonstrators and security personnel, leaving people on both sides injured. That clash has already become a political flashpoint this week, with opposition leader Rahul Gandhi accusing Home Minister Amit Shah of ordering students to be shot at, a charge the government denies — so this Supreme Court case is the judicial track of a story that's also playing out as a political fight in Parliament.

stories.title: Alex Albon pinpoints what's really holding Williams back in its rocky 2026 season
stories.what_happened: Alex Albon gave a candid assessment of Williams' 2026 season, saying the team's underperformance isn't the result of one clear technical flaw but rather **'a bit of everything'** — a combination of smaller issues across the car rather than a single fixable weakness. He specifically flagged the car's weakness in **high-speed corners**, noting 'if you look at our high speed compared to our midfield rivals, we're a good chunk off' — a deficit that hurt both him and teammate Carlos Sainz at the Barcelona race weekend. Albon also described the knock-on effect on his qualifying performances, saying that without confidence in how the car would behave, he found himself 'having to drive it like a race lap' in qualifying rather than pushing to the limit, adding 'left to right, corner to corner, I didn't know what the car was going to do.' He summarised the team's broader position as being **'on the back foot'** as rival midfield teams continue to bring development upgrades that Williams has struggled to match.
key_points: Albon says Williams' struggles aren't down to **one single flaw** but **'a bit of everything'** across the car.
The **FW48 is notably off the pace in high-speed corners**, a weakness that hurt both Albon and teammate Carlos Sainz badly in Barcelona.
Albon described **not knowing what the car would do** 'left to right, corner to corner' during recent qualifying sessions.
Williams has fallen **'on the back foot'** in the 2026 in-season development race as rivals continue upgrading.
The team says it's aware of the issues and is working through **an extensive list of fixes**.

depth.background: Williams, one of F1's oldest teams, has spent recent seasons rebuilding after years near the back of the grid, with **Alex Albon** as a key part of that recovery story. The 2026 season's all-new technical rules gave every team a fresh start, and Williams hoped its rebuilding work would translate into a stronger midfield or even points-challenging car — but a shaky start and ongoing development struggles have made that harder than expected.

stories.title: China's free Kimi K3 model rockets to No. 1 on a major AI coding leaderboard, beating Anthropic and OpenAI's best
stories.what_happened: Moonshot AI released Kimi K3's weights for free on **July 26**, a 2.8-trillion-parameter model that instantly became the largest open-source AI model ever released. Within days, independent benchmarking on Arena.ai's Frontend Code leaderboard — which tests how well models build real user-facing software — showed Kimi K3 jumping from 18th place (as the older Kimi-K2.6) straight to **1st**, ahead of Anthropic's Claude Fable 5, OpenAI's GPT-5.6, and xAI's Grok-4.5. It ranked first in six of seven measured categories, including data/analytics tools and consumer product design, trailing only in gaming-related tasks. The release reignited a policy debate: on July 27, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei addressed it directly, saying his company has **'never advocated for a ban on open-weights models'** and views safe open releases as beneficial, even as US labs race to stay ahead on the frontier.
key_points: Kimi K3, from Chinese lab **Moonshot AI**, jumped **17 places** to take **#1** on Arena.ai's Frontend Code leaderboard.
It's a **2.8-trillion-parameter** open-weights model — meaning anyone can download and run it for free, unlike closed rivals.
It outscored **Claude Fable 5**, GPT-5.6, and Grok-4.5 on the same benchmark, ranking first in 6 of 7 tested skill areas.
Anthropic CEO **Dario Amodei** publicly responded, calling non-dangerous open models **'a public good'** rather than backing a ban.
It ships with a **1-million-token context window**, letting it read roughly the length of several novels in one go.

depth.background: For the past two years, the most capable AI models — the ones best at writing code, reasoning, and holding long conversations — have come from a handful of US labs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google) and stayed closed, meaning you pay to access them through an API but can't download or inspect them. China's AI labs, including Moonshot AI, DeepSeek, and Alibaba, have taken the opposite approach: releasing **'open-weights'** models that anyone can download, modify, and run on their own hardware for free. Each new Chinese open release has narrowed the gap with US frontier models a little further, feeding a running debate in Washington over whether that's a security risk or a healthy counterweight to a handful of companies controlling the most powerful AI.

stories.title: IMD issues a red alert as a 'deep depression' dumps extreme rain on Odisha, Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh
stories.what_happened: The **India Meteorological Department (IMD)** issued a **red alert for Odisha and Chhattisgarh**, warning that a deep depression crossing the region could dump **isolated extremely heavy rainfall exceeding 204.5mm in a day** — enough to cause flash floods, waterlogging and landslides in vulnerable areas. As of the IMD's Thursday bulletin, the system was centered over **west-central Chhattisgarh and adjoining Vidarbha and southeast Madhya Pradesh**, moving westward and expected to weaken into a depression and then a low-pressure area over the next day or so. The IMD separately warned that torrential rain and thunderstorms will continue for the **next seven days across more than 20 states**, including Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand and swathes of North India, as this system interacts with a second weather pattern. The alert comes on top of an already damaging monsoon season, with flood tolls rising in Assam and landslides blocking 150+ roads in Himachal Pradesh in recent days.
key_points: India's weather office (**IMD**) issued a **red alert** — its highest warning level — for **Odisha and Chhattisgarh** as a deep depression crosses the region.
Isolated pockets could see **over 204.5mm of rain** in a single day, enough to trigger flash floods and landslides.
The depression is moving **westward across Chhattisgarh** and is expected to weaken gradually over the next 24-48 hours.
The IMD warns that heavy to very heavy rain will hit **more than 20 states**, including Madhya Pradesh, Vidarbha (Maharashtra), Jharkhand and North India, over the coming week.
This adds to an already active monsoon that has caused flooding in Assam and landslides in Himachal Pradesh in recent days.

depth.background: A 'deep depression' is one step below a cyclone on India's monsoon storm-intensity scale — a large, organized low-pressure system that draws in huge amounts of moisture and dumps it as intense rain over whatever land it crosses. Central and eastern India — states like Odisha, Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh — regularly see several of these systems form over the Bay of Bengal each monsoon season, and they're a major driver of both the farm-friendly rain India's economy depends on and the flash floods that displace people every year.

stories.title: Charles Leclerc tells Ferrari: stay 'aggressive' in F1's upgrade arms race or lose the title fight
stories.what_happened: Speaking after a difficult **Hungarian Grand Prix weekend**, Charles Leclerc told Ferrari's management that the team must not slow down its pace of car development, describing 2026 as an 'upgrade arms race' in which each new part can produce a large jump in performance — meaning any team that eases off risks falling behind fast. Leclerc said he had a **'strange' feeling** driving the current SF-26 car and stressed the importance of Ferrari staying as aggressive with upgrades as it has been all year. Ferrari has already introduced significant upgrade packages at the **Miami and Barcelona** races and a **new engine at the Austrian Grand Prix**, making it one of the most upgrade-heavy teams on the 2026 grid. The team is now preparing a **new aerodynamic package for the Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort**, followed by a **power-unit upgrade at Monza**, Ferrari's home race in Italy. Despite all this investment, Ferrari sits **72 points behind Mercedes** in the constructors' championship heading into F1's summer break, because rival teams have continued developing at a similarly aggressive pace, blunting the relative gains Ferrari hoped its upgrades would deliver.
key_points: Leclerc says Ferrari must not relent in bringing new car upgrades, calling 2026 an **'upgrade arms race'** where falling behind for even one weekend costs dearly.
Ferrari is currently **72 points behind** constructors' championship leaders Mercedes heading into the summer break.
Ferrari has already brought **major upgrade packages at Miami, Barcelona, and a new engine in Austria** — among the most aggressive development pushes on the grid.
Big upgrades are planned for **Zandvoort** (aerodynamics) and **Monza**, Ferrari's home race (a new power-unit upgrade).
Leclerc described a **'strange' feeling** with the current SF-26 car after a tough Hungarian Grand Prix weekend.

depth.background: Formula 1's 2026 season runs under a **major new set of technical regulations** — new engine rules and car designs — which reset the competitive order and made in-season development (bringing new parts to the car race by race) unusually important, since every team is still learning how to optimise the new rules. Ferrari has spent the year locked in a tight title fight and has tried to out-develop rivals by bringing upgrades more frequently than most teams, but rivals like Mercedes, Red Bull, and McLaren have kept pace, meaning Ferrari's gains haven't translated into a clear championship lead.

stories.title: Oliver Bearman says Lewis Hamilton's Ferrari revival is 'special' to watch — but it's closing his own door to Maranello
stories.what_happened: Bearman said publicly that watching Hamilton's improved form in 2026 has been **"special"** to see, given Hamilton's stature in the sport, but conceded it is **"not ideal"** for his own career timeline, since a settled, high-performing Hamilton-Leclerc pairing leaves no obvious seat for Bearman to move into. Bearman has continued to build his own case regardless, consistently outperforming Haas teammate Esteban Ocon through the 2026 season. Ferrari's presumed intention to continue with both Hamilton and Leclerc into 2027 means Bearman's Ferrari promotion, once seen as increasingly likely, now looks like it will have to wait at least another year.
key_points: **Haas driver Oliver Bearman**, a Ferrari Driver Academy graduate, admitted **Lewis Hamilton's 2026 resurgence at Ferrari** is impressive but **"not ideal"** for his own promotion hopes.
Hamilton struggled through a difficult **first season at Ferrari in 2025**, which had made a Bearman promotion look more realistic.
Hamilton's much-improved 2026 form has **strengthened the case for Ferrari keeping its current line-up** of Hamilton and Charles Leclerc into 2027.
Bearman continues to **outperform teammate Esteban Ocon** at Haas, building his case for a future promotion even without an immediate opening.
Ferrari is widely expected to have **no vacant seat for 2027**, pushing any Bearman move further into the future.

depth.background: **Oliver Bearman** is a product of the **Ferrari Driver Academy**, the young-driver pipeline Ferrari uses to develop future stars, and was placed at **Haas** — a team that effectively runs Ferrari engines and has close ties to the Italian marque — to gain full-season experience before a potential promotion to the main Ferrari team. That path looked more open after **Lewis Hamilton's rocky debut season at Ferrari in 2025**, his first after leaving Mercedes, which raised questions about how long the seven-time champion would hold his seat. Ferrari's other seat is held by **Charles Leclerc**, who has been with the team since 2019.

stories.title: Gaza ceasefire talks in Cairo see 'rare progress' as Hamas discusses giving up weapons
stories.what_happened: Egyptian sources say Hamas has agreed to several previously disputed points in the Cairo talks, including a **process for transferring both heavy and light weapons**, though it is pushing back on Israel's definition of which infrastructure counts as military and must be torn down. A Hamas official and a diplomat close to the talks described the discussions as 'positive' and 'making progress' — a notably more upbeat tone than prior rounds. An unnamed Israeli official said Israel had rejected one of the proposals on the table, underlining that a deal is not yet close. Meanwhile, Israeli strikes on Thursday killed at least **four Palestinians, including two children**, adding to a toll of more than 1,200 people killed since the ceasefire nominally began.
key_points: Mediators say the Cairo talks are making **'rare progress'** toward fully implementing the US-brokered Gaza peace plan.
Hamas has reportedly agreed to **several disputed points**, including a process for handing over weapons.
The sides are still stuck on **how to define which infrastructure** must be dismantled.
Israeli strikes **killed at least four people, including two children**, in Gaza even as the talks continued.
More than **1,200 Palestinians** have died in Israeli strikes since the ceasefire technically took effect, per Gaza health officials.

depth.background: Gaza has been under a fragile, repeatedly-violated ceasefire tied to President Trump's peace plan, which is being implemented in phases and overseen by a body called the 'Board of Peace'. A recurring sticking point has been Hamas's weapons — Israel wants the group fully disarmed as a condition for winding down its own operations, while Hamas has resisted full decommissioning without guarantees on its own terms. Egypt, Qatar, and Türkiye have been the main mediators shuttling between the two sides in Cairo.

stories.title: A 24-year-old's $45 billion AI hedge fund collapses to $10 billion in days as a leveraged AI bet unwinds
stories.what_happened: On **July 30**, Situational Awareness LP sold the bulk of its public stock holdings to Citadel after **margin calls from three prime brokers** hit a portfolio leveraged about **four times over**. The fund had ridden AI-infrastructure names like SK Hynix to a **439% gain in the first half of 2026**, but a sharp reversal in AI-networking and semiconductor stocks — Marvell Technology alone fell **over 40%** between late June and July 30 — wiped out most of those gains. Aschenbrenner had told investors on July 24 the sell-off was a buying opportunity and invited fresh capital by August 1, but no new money arrived in time. By Thursday morning, the leverage that amplified the fund's gains amplified its losses instead, and both legs of the trade unwound simultaneously. What remains — about **$10 billion**, including a **$5 billion Anthropic stake** — will keep operating as a smaller, private vehicle.
key_points: Situational Awareness LP, run by 24-year-old ex-OpenAI researcher **Leopold Aschenbrenner**, shrank from **$45 billion to about $10 billion** in a matter of days.
The fund was leveraged roughly **4x**, going long AI-infrastructure stocks like SK Hynix while shorting software incumbents like Adobe — both bets unwound at once.
Three prime brokers — **Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan and Bank of America** — issued margin calls on Thursday, forcing a fire-sale.
**Ken Griffin's Citadel** bought the bulk of the stock portfolio; the fund had been up **439%** in the first half of the year before losing **~67%** in July alone.
The fund keeps a **$5 billion stake in Anthropic** and will now operate as a smaller, private investment vehicle.

depth.background: Leopold Aschenbrenner is a former OpenAI safety researcher who became a hedge-fund manager after publishing an influential essay arguing AI progress would be far faster than most expected. His fund, Situational Awareness LP, turned that thesis into a trade: borrow heavily to bet big on the companies building AI infrastructure — chips, memory, data centers — while betting against software firms he expected AI to disrupt. **CNBC's Jim Cramer publicly warned viewers on July 28** to exit leveraged data-center trades, just two days before the fund's positions began to unravel.

stories.title: F1 paddock mourns Aston Martin's long-serving tyre technician Mick 'Biscuit' Fern, dead after 35 years in the sport
stories.what_happened: **Aston Martin** confirmed that **Mick Fern**, the team's long-serving tyre technician known as **'Biscuit'**, died after privately battling an off-track illness. Fern had spent **35 years in the Formula 1 paddock**, first joining in 1999 when the Silverstone-based team competed as **Jordan**, before rejoining in **2015** in his most recent stint. For the past **seven seasons** he had been responsible for **Lance Stroll's tyres** on every race weekend. Fern was notably absent from the recent **Hungarian Grand Prix** due to his illness, prompting the team to display a sign outside their garage reading **'Biscuit. Thinking of you'** in support. Following his death, Aston Martin described him as **'a true stalwart'** who was **'respected by all who worked with him.'** Stroll posted an emotional personal tribute, thanking him for **'7 years of getting my tyres race-ready,'** and other drivers including **Esteban Ocon and Fernando Alonso** also shared condolences.
key_points: **Mick Fern**, known throughout the paddock as **'Biscuit'**, died after what Aston Martin described as a private off-track battle with illness.
He spent **35 years in Formula 1**, joining the team's predecessor **Jordan back in 1999** before rejoining the Silverstone-based squad (now Aston Martin) in 2015.
As **Lance Stroll's tyre technician for the past 7 seasons**, he was a fixture in the garage every race weekend.
Fern **missed the Hungarian Grand Prix** due to illness; the team had placed a sign outside the garage reading **'Biscuit. Thinking of you.'**
Tributes poured in from across the paddock, including **Lance Stroll, Esteban Ocon and Fernando Alonso**.

depth.background: Behind every F1 driver is a small army of mechanics and technicians who travel the world race weekend after race weekend, largely out of the spotlight — tyre technicians in particular are responsible for the split-second tyre changes that decide pit-stop times and races. Mick Fern was one of the longest-serving members of this crew, having worked in the paddock since 1999 under the team's various guises: Jordan, then later incarnations through to today's **Aston Martin**. His nickname 'Biscuit' and decades of continuity made him a familiar, well-liked figure across rival teams, not just his own.

stories.title: Red Bull's own outgoing boss says he wouldn't bet on Max Verstappen winning the 2026 title
stories.what_happened: Speaking about Red Bull's 2026 season, Helmut Marko said he would not bet on Max Verstappen mounting a serious title challenge this year, citing the team's **inconsistent pace**, an **unstable car**, and growing friction between Verstappen and his race engineers as obstacles he sees as insurmountable this season. Verstappen is currently **sixth** in the drivers' standings and has yet to win a single grand prix in 2026, a stark contrast to his four-title run through 2021-2024 and his close title fight in 2025. Marko's comments come as he prepares to leave his long-standing Red Bull role at the end of this year, and as Verstappen's own contract is reported to include performance-linked exit clauses tied to his standing in the championship.
key_points: Red Bull motorsport advisor **Helmut Marko** says he wouldn't wager money on Verstappen fighting for the 2026 title.
Marko cited Red Bull's **inconsistent pace**, an unstable car, and tension between Verstappen and his engineers.
Verstappen sits **sixth** in the drivers' championship with **zero wins** so far in 2026.
Marko is leaving Red Bull's F1 project **at the end of this year** after a 25-year stint.
Verstappen lost the 2025 title to Lando Norris by just **two points** in Abu Dhabi.

depth.background: Helmut Marko has been one of Red Bull's most influential F1 figures for 25 years, overseeing its driver programme and playing a central role in Max Verstappen's rise to four world championships. Verstappen narrowly lost the 2025 title to McLaren's Lando Norris by two points, and 2026 introduced a major new set of technical regulations that reshuffled the competitive order — Red Bull has struggled to adapt as well as rivals like McLaren and Mercedes. Marko announced earlier this year that he is stepping back from his Red Bull role at the end of the 2026 season.

stories.title: ICC confirms 12 venues across South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia for the 2027 World Cup
stories.what_happened: The ICC officially unveiled the 12 venues for the 2027 Men's Cricket World Cup at a launch event in Johannesburg. South Africa will host the bulk of matches across 8 grounds — Wanderers Stadium (Johannesburg), SuperSport Park (Centurion), Newlands (Cape Town), Kingsmead (Durban), St George's Park (Gqeberha), Mangaung Oval (Bloemfontein), Boland Park (Paarl) and Buffalo Park (KuGompo City, formerly East London). Zimbabwe will host games at Harare Sports Club, Queens Sports Club (Bulawayo) and the Victoria Falls stadium. Namibia's Windhoek ground will also host matches. The tournament will run as a 50-over competition with 14 teams playing 57 matches in total.
key_points: The ICC has confirmed **12 host venues** for the 2027 Men's Cricket World Cup.
Matches will be split across **South Africa (8 venues), Zimbabwe (3) and Namibia (1)**.
It's a **50-over tournament** featuring **14 teams and 57 matches**.
The World Cup returns to **Africa for the first time in 24 years**.
The venues and tournament brand were revealed at a **launch event in Johannesburg**.

depth.background: The Cricket World Cup is the sport's flagship 50-over (One Day International) tournament, held roughly every four years. Africa last hosted the men's World Cup in 2003 (South Africa, Zimbabwe and Kenya), so this 2027 edition marks a long-awaited return of the tournament to the continent. Confirming host venues years in advance lets host boards plan stadium upgrades, ticketing, and broadcast infrastructure, and gives fans and travelling teams a clear roadmap.

stories.title: Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli to skip the 2026 Duleep Trophy, pushing their next India appearance to late September
stories.what_happened: Reports confirmed that neither **Rohit Sharma** nor **Virat Kohli** will play in this year's **Duleep Trophy**, which starts **August 23, 2026**, meaning fans won't see the pair turn out in India colours again until the **ODI series against the West Indies**, which begins **September 27** at the **Greenfield International Stadium** in Thiruvananthapuram. The news followed Rohit's **century in the third and final ODI against England at Lord's**, a match India lost by 27 runs, with England taking the series 2-1 — a performance that quieted some retirement speculation even as the series was lost. Former teammate **Ravichandran Ashwin** weighed in publicly in support of both players, arguing they cannot simply be dropped while they're still contributing at this level, pointing to their combined record of more than 8,000 ODI runs together across 21 century partnerships.
key_points: **Rohit Sharma** and **Virat Kohli** will **not feature** in the 2026 Duleep Trophy, which begins **August 23**.
Their next appearance in India colours is set to be the **ODI series against West Indies**, starting **September 27** at Thiruvananthapuram.
The decision comes after Rohit's **century at Lord's** in the third ODI against England — a match India still **lost by 27 runs**, going down **2-1** in the series.
Former India spinner **Ravichandran Ashwin** publicly backed the pair, saying the two senior batters **"cannot simply be dropped"** if they still want to play for India.
Rohit and Kohli have now put together more than **8,000 ODI runs together** across **21 century stands**.

depth.background: **Rohit Sharma** and **Virat Kohli** are two of India's most decorated batters, and questions about how much longer they'll continue playing for India have intensified as both have scaled back their involvement in India's longer domestic and franchise commitments. The **Duleep Trophy** is a first-class domestic tournament used partly to help fringe and returning players sharpen their red-ball form — a tournament senior international players don't always need to play. Rohit's recent **Lord's century**, even in a losing effort, had reignited debate over whether the veteran pair still has a long-term role in India's plans.

stories.title: Stephen Fleming named England's new Test coach as Joe Root returns as captain
stories.what_happened: The England and Wales Cricket Board announced Stephen Fleming, 52, as the new England men's Test head coach — his first job leading a national team, after an 18-year association with Chennai Super Kings in the IPL. He replaces Brendon McCullum, sacked in June. Fleming has signed a four-year deal that runs until the end of September 2030. Alongside the coaching change, **Joe Root has been reappointed England Test captain**, returning to a role he left in 2022. Fleming will not take over immediately — he'll start after England's series against Pakistan begins, with Marcus Trescothick serving as interim head coach in the meantime.
key_points: The **ECB** has named former New Zealand captain **Stephen Fleming** as England's new men's Test head coach.
**Joe Root** returns as Test captain, a role he left back in **2022**.
Fleming replaces **Brendon McCullum**, who was sacked in June after poor results and off-field issues.
Fleming signed a **four-year deal running through September 2030**.
He won't start immediately — **Marcus Trescothick** is interim coach until after the Pakistan series begins.

depth.background: England's Test team has been going through turbulence: head coach Brendon McCullum, who oversaw the aggressive 'Bazball' era, was sacked in June 2026 following a run of poor results and off-field incidents. Stephen Fleming is one of the most respected figures in world cricket — New Zealand's most successful Test captain across 111 matches, and more recently the long-serving, highly rated head coach of Chennai Super Kings in the IPL for 18 years, a role he only just left. Joe Root previously captained England's Test side until 2022, when he stepped down and Ben Stokes took over — Root staying on as the team's best batter throughout.

stories.title: Adrian Newey says he's 'confident' Fernando Alonso stays at Aston Martin, as Alpine circles for 2027
stories.what_happened: Speaking in Hungary, **Adrian Newey** addressed what Alonso's potential departure would mean for Aston Martin, saying Alonso 'brings huge amounts to the team, both in his feedback and his ability,' and that he is 'pretty confident' the relationship will continue. This comes as rumours grow that Alonso could make a surprise return to **Alpine** for 2027, with Briatore and Alpine's incoming title sponsor reportedly pushing hard to sign him. Alonso himself has not decided, and is believed to be waiting until after the summer break to see whether Aston Martin's upgrades — including a near-complete new chassis — lift the team's form. Briatore, asked directly about an Alpine reunion, didn't rule it out but said Alonso remains 'an Aston Martin driver' through the end of the season.
key_points: Alonso is contracted at Aston Martin only through the **end of this season**, with no deal yet for 2027.
Newey says he's **'pretty confident'** Alonso will stay, calling him 'an amazing driver.'
Alonso's long-time manager **Flavio Briatore**, now an Alpine executive advisor, is pushing hard to bring him back for a fourth stint.
Alonso is reportedly waiting until **after the summer break** to decide, hoping Aston Martin's upgrades show real progress.
Aston Martin has scored just **one point** from the season's first 11 races.

depth.background: Fernando Alonso is a two-time world champion who joined **Aston Martin** in 2023 partly on the promise that design legend **Adrian Newey** — hired as the team's managing technical partner in 2025 — would eventually build him a genuinely competitive car. So far in 2026, that hasn't happened: Aston Martin has struggled at the back of the grid. Alonso has history with **Alpine** (formerly Renault), where he won both his championships in 2005-06 under team boss **Flavio Briatore**, who now holds an advisory role at Alpine and is reportedly keen to reunite with his old driver for what would be Alonso's farewell season.

stories.title: Neeraj Chopra opens his Commonwealth Games javelin title defense in Glasgow qualifying
stories.what_happened: The men's javelin throw qualifying round is being held today in Glasgow, part of the athletics program at the **2026 Commonwealth Games**. Chopra needs to hit an automatic qualifying distance or finish among the top throwers to advance to Friday's medal round. He goes in with strong recent form, having thrown **85.69m** for fourth place at the Doha Diamond League — a distance well above what's typically needed to advance. India has entered three men in the event: Chopra, Yash Vir Singh, and Rohit Yadav. The final will take place in the early hours of **August 1 (IST)**.
key_points: Chopra begins his bid to **reclaim the men's javelin title** he won at **Gold Coast 2018**, in today's qualifying round in Glasgow.
He **missed Birmingham 2022** with injury, making this his first CWG javelin appearance in **eight years**.
He arrives in form, having thrown **85.69m for fourth place** at the Doha Diamond League, well clear of the qualifying mark.
Fellow Indians **Yash Vir Singh and Rohit Yadav** also compete in the qualifying round alongside him.
The **final is in the early hours of August 1 (IST)** — a two-day wait after today's qualifying.

depth.background: **Neeraj Chopra** is India's most decorated track and field athlete, best known for winning India's first-ever Olympic gold in athletics at Tokyo 2020. He won Commonwealth Games javelin gold at **Gold Coast in 2018**, but a groin injury forced him out of the **2022 Birmingham Games** entirely, leaving him without a CWG title defense until now. Since then he has remained one of the world's most consistent javelin throwers, competing for global and Olympic medals against rivals including Pakistan's Arshad Nadeem.

stories.title: Parliament takes up a bill to expand the Supreme Court from 33 to 37 judges, replacing a May ordinance
stories.what_happened: The **Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026**, which raises the court's judge count from **33 to 37** (not counting the Chief Justice of India), was introduced in the Lok Sabha on **July 20** by Law Minister **Arjun Ram Meghwal**, and the House took it up for consideration and passage on **Thursday, July 30**. The bill formally replaces an **ordinance the government had already issued on May 16, 2026** to expand the court before Parliament reconvened. Opposition MPs Sougata Ray, N.K. Premachandran, and Dean Kuriakose used a **statutory resolution** — a parliamentary tool to formally object to a government ordinance — to challenge the original move, arguing it should have gone through Parliament first rather than being enacted by executive order.
key_points: The **Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026** would raise the court's sanctioned strength (excluding the Chief Justice) from **33 to 37 judges**.
It **replaces an ordinance** the government had already issued on **May 16, 2026** to make the change immediately, before Parliament could vote on it.
The **Lok Sabha took up the bill on Thursday**, July 30, as part of the ongoing Monsoon Session.
Opposition MPs **Sougata Ray, N.K. Premachandran, and Dean Kuriakose** moved a statutory resolution seeking to **disapprove of the original ordinance**.
The government says more judges will help the Supreme Court **clear its backlog and deliver faster justice**.

depth.background: India's Supreme Court has for years struggled with a **massive case backlog** — tens of thousands of pending cases — partly because its sanctioned judge strength hasn't kept pace with the volume of appeals reaching it. When Parliament isn't in session, the government can issue an **ordinance** — a temporary law with the force of legislation — to act quickly, but ordinances **must be replaced by a proper law within six months** or they lapse. The government used this route in May 2026 to expand the court immediately, and is now asking Parliament to formally convert that ordinance into permanent law.

stories.title: US economy grows just 1.5% in Q2, badly missing forecasts and signaling a real slowdown
stories.what_happened: The Bureau of Economic Analysis's advance estimate showed real (inflation-adjusted) GDP grew at a **1.5% annualized rate** in Q2 2026 (April-June), missing the **2.1%** consensus forecast and down from **2.1%** growth in Q1. The BEA said the deceleration reflected a **downturn in government spending** and slower investment and exports, only partly offset by **stronger consumer spending**. Alongside the growth miss, the inflation detail in the report was hot: the price index for gross domestic purchases rose **5.7%**, up sharply from 3.6% in Q1, and the core PCE price index (the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, excluding food and energy) came in elevated too. The report followed Wednesday's Fed decision to hold its benchmark rate at 3.50%-3.75% on a 9-3 vote, with dissenting officials Beth Hammack, Neel Kashkari, and Lorie Logan wanting to raise rates instead because of persistent above-target inflation.
key_points: US GDP (the total value of everything the economy produced) grew at an annualized **1.5%** in Q2 2026, well below the **2.1%** economists expected.
That's a clear **deceleration from Q1's 2.1%** growth — the economy is losing momentum, not gaining it.
Consumer spending actually **picked up speed**, but a drop in **government spending** and slower investment and exports dragged the headline number down.
Inflation pressure in the report **got worse, not better**: the price index for domestic purchases jumped to **5.7%** from 3.6% in Q1.
The data lands one day after the **Fed held interest rates steady**, with three officials wanting a hike instead — this report makes that call look prescient, not overly cautious.

depth.background: GDP (Gross Domestic Product) is the broadest scorecard for an economy — the total value of goods and services produced in a period, reported at an 'annualized' rate so quarters can be compared like-for-like. The US Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) publishes an 'advance estimate' about a month after each quarter ends, using partial data that often gets revised later. Coming into this report, the story on Wall Street had been that the US economy was 'resilient' despite tariffs, high rates, and the Iran conflict earlier this year. This print is the first hard evidence that the resilience narrative is cracking, arriving just a day after the **Federal Reserve voted 9-3 to hold rates at 3.50%-3.75%**, with three regional Fed presidents dissenting in favor of a hike because inflation has stayed above the Fed's 2% target for **more than five years**.

stories.title: Honda explains the mysterious engine 'oscillations' that alarmed Alonso in Hungary — and says it's fixed
stories.what_happened: During **first practice** at the Hungarian Grand Prix, Fernando Alonso radioed in about unusual **oscillations** in his Aston Martin's engine at high speed in seventh gear. Honda's engineers investigated and identified the cause as an **engine combustion characteristic** linked to how engine temperature behaved in the car's new chassis — a distinct issue from the vibration problems the team faced earlier in the season. Honda's Shintaro Orihara confirmed the team adjusted engine parameters between first and second practice and made 'good progress' resolving it. Honda says it is confident these **corrective measures** have dispelled Alonso's complaints.
key_points: Alonso reported strange **oscillations** in seventh gear on Hungary's main straight in first practice.
Honda says the cause was an **engine combustion characteristic** tied to engine temperature, not a repeat of earlier vibration problems.
Honda made **corrective adjustments** between practice sessions and says the issue was resolved.
This is a **different fault** from the vibration issue that plagued the Aston Martin-Honda power unit earlier in 2026.
Honda's next-generation engine upgrade is due to debut at the **Dutch Grand Prix**.

depth.background: Aston Martin switched to **Honda** engines for the 2026 season as part of its wider technical rebuild alongside hiring Adrian Newey, but the partnership has been dogged by reliability scares, including an earlier vibration problem severe enough that Alonso said he lost feeling in his limbs. **Trackside general manager Shintaro Orihara** leads Honda's on-the-ground engineering response to issues like these during race weekends.

stories.title: Aston Martin's Adrian Newey lays out the Honda-powered comeback plan — and what it means for Alonso's future
stories.what_happened: Aston Martin brought a substantial package of car upgrades to the **Hungarian Grand Prix**, its last race before F1's summer break, and Fernando Alonso reached **Q2 on pure pace for the first time this season** as a result. Team principal **Adrian Newey** confirmed that further upgrades to the **AMR26** are planned for the **Netherlands Grand Prix at Zandvoort**, with additional developments layered in at **Monza and Baku** later in the year — effectively a staged recovery plan through the back half of the season. On the engine side, Aston Martin and power-unit partner **Honda** have held a series of direct, admittedly **'tough' conversations** after it emerged Honda had reassigned many of its Formula 1 specialists to other projects while ramping up its return to the sport — a key reason the power unit underperformed early on. Both sides say the talks have improved their working relationship, with a **major power-unit upgrade** due once the summer break ends. Newey also addressed what **Alonso's future** at the team means for Aston Martin's trajectory, as the two-time champion — contracted through the end of 2026 — is expected to announce a decision on his future during the break.
key_points: Aston Martin brought a **major package of upgrades** to the Hungarian Grand Prix, and **Fernando Alonso reached Q2 on pace for the first time all season**.
Team boss **Adrian Newey** confirmed **further upgrades are coming at Zandvoort, then more at Monza and Baku** — a staged comeback plan through the second half of 2026.
The team's **Honda power unit** was the season's biggest weak point after Aston discovered Honda had reassigned many of its F1 specialists elsewhere while ramping up its return to the sport.
Aston Martin and Honda have since held **'tough' but relationship-repairing meetings**, with a major power-unit upgrade due after the summer break.

Two-time champion **Alonso is contracted through the end of 2026** and is expected to decide his future during the summer break — Newey has now spoken publicly about what his eventual departure would mean for the team.

depth.background: Aston Martin entered the 2026 season with sky-high expectations after hiring legendary designer **Adrian Newey** — architect of multiple championship-winning cars at Red Bull and elsewhere — and forming a new partnership with engine-maker **Honda**, which returned to Formula 1 this year. Early results badly lagged expectations, largely because Honda's power unit underperformed; it later emerged that Honda had spread its F1 engineering talent thin while managing its comeback. **Fernando Alonso**, a two-time world champion, joined Aston Martin partly on the promise that Newey's arrival would eventually deliver a genuinely competitive car — a promise that, halfway through 2026, hadn't yet materialized on track.

stories.title: Bumrah's rest period ends today — he reports to the BCCI's Centre of Excellence for the next fitness check
stories.what_happened: Bumrah tore a ligament in his left knee during a collision in the second ODI against England at Cardiff, causing reactive swelling that ruled him out of the series-deciding third ODI at Lord's. He has been in a structured rehabilitation program and was scheduled to rest until **July 30 — today** — after which he reports to the BCCI's Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru for the next phase of assessment. His participation in the Sri Lanka Test series remains conditional on fitness: the first Test starts in Galle on **August 15** and the second in Colombo on **August 23**. The real test of his readiness comes at a practice match in Colombo on **August 7**, which selectors are treating as the deciding checkpoint. Should Bumrah not be ready, India's fallback pace options are Mohammed Siraj, uncapped left-armer Gurnoor Brar, and Prasidh Krishna.
key_points: **Jasprit Bumrah's** rest period for a torn left knee ligament ends **today, July 30** — he now reports to the BCCI's Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru.
The injury happened during the **2nd ODI vs England at Cardiff**, and forced him to miss the series-deciding Lord's ODI.
His fitness determines whether he plays the **Sri Lanka Test series** — 1st Test in Galle from August 15, 2nd in Colombo from August 23.
A practice match in Colombo on **August 7** is the real checkpoint that will decide his availability.
If he isn't ready, **Mohammed Siraj, Gurnoor Brar and Prasidh Krishna** are the fallback pace options.

depth.background: Bumrah is India's premier fast bowler and has a long history of carefully managed workload and injuries, including a back stress fracture that sidelined him for the better part of a year in 2023. He suffered a knee injury during India's tour of England this July, forcing selectors to plan around his possible absence for the upcoming tour of Sri Lanka. Given his central role in India's bowling attack, his fitness status has been one of the most closely tracked storylines on the Indian cricket calendar this month.

stories.title: Supreme Court rules a wife's property stays hers alone, even after death, in landmark Christian inheritance case
stories.what_happened: Ruling on July 30 in Shakunatala & Ors. v. Robert Anthony & Ors., the Supreme Court held that when a husband purchases property in his wife's name, that property is legally hers — full stop — regardless of who paid for it. Upon her death, the court said, succession to that property must follow from her ownership and her legal heirs, and Section 33 of the Indian Succession Act (which governs distribution of a person's own estate) cannot be used to instead route it through the husband's estate. The ruling directly addressed a dispute where relatives had argued the property should be treated as part of the husband's assets for inheritance purposes.
key_points: The Supreme Court ruled that property a **husband buys in his wife's name** legally belongs to **her alone**.
On her death, that property passes under **her** succession rights — it is **not** treated as part of the husband's estate.
The case, **Shakunatala & Ors. v. Robert Anthony & Ors.**, specifically clarifies **Christian succession law** in India.
It stops relatives from claiming such property should be divided under the **husband's** inheritance rules instead of the wife's.

depth.background: India doesn't have a single inheritance law for everyone — different religious communities follow different succession codes, and Christians in India are governed by the Indian Succession Act, 1925. A recurring source of family property disputes is what happens when a husband buys property but registers it in his wife's name: after her death, do her own legal heirs inherit it, or can it be swept into the husband's estate and divided among his heirs instead? Section 33 of the Act governs how a deceased person's property is distributed among a spouse and children, and its application has been contested when ownership itself is unclear.

stories.title: Ajinkya Rahane retires from international cricket, closing a 12-year career defined by the 2020-21 Adelaide comeback
stories.what_happened: Rahane confirmed his retirement from international cricket in all formats on Thursday, writing on social media, 'Today, I feel the timing is right for me to move on and announce my retirement from international cricket and all formats.' He ends his 12-year international career with 5,077 Test runs at an average of 38.46, including 12 centuries, along with 2,962 ODI runs and 375 T20I runs. His most recent international appearance was a Test match in the West Indies in July 2023, meaning this retirement formalizes what had effectively already become the end of his playing days for India.
key_points: Rahane announced retirement from **all formats** of international cricket via social media on Thursday.
He finishes with **5,077 Test runs at 38.46** with **12 centuries** across **85 Tests**, plus 90 ODIs and 20 T20Is.
He led India to a **historic 2-1 Test series win in Australia (2020-21)**, days after India was bowled out for **36** in the series opener.
His last international match was a **Test in the West Indies in July 2023**.
His career spanned **2011 to 2023**, including stints as vice-captain and stand-in captain.

depth.background: **Ajinkya Rahane** was a mainstay of India's middle order through the 2010s, known for his calm temperament under pressure. His signature moment came during India's tour of Australia in 2020-21: after India was bowled out for a humiliating **36 runs** in the series-opening Test — its lowest-ever Test total — Rahane took over as stand-in captain (with Virat Kohli away for the birth of his child) and led India to a stunning **2-1 series win**, one of the most celebrated comebacks in modern Test cricket. He hadn't played for India since mid-2023.

stories.title: F1 confirms an Imola/Europe fallback for its season finale if the Qatar and Abu Dhabi races can't happen
stories.what_happened: In a round-up of F1 news published Thursday, Domenicali confirmed for the first time that the series has a concrete fallback plan: if Qatar and Abu Dhabi cannot be held safely, the season would instead close out with a race in **Europe**, with **Imola** — Italy's Emilia Romagna circuit — the venue most commonly tipped to step in. The update follows Tuesday's escalation, in which Iran's Revolutionary Guard fired ballistic missiles directly at a US base in Jordan for the first time since Washington paused its own strikes, intensifying fears that the wider region could remain a war zone through the scheduled November-December race dates.
key_points: F1 president **Stefano Domenicali** confirmed the championship would finish in **Europe** if the Qatar and Abu Dhabi races can't go ahead.
**Imola** is being tipped as the likely replacement venue for the season finale.
The contingency plan follows this week's **direct Iranian missile attack on a US base in Jordan**, deepening doubts over racing in the Gulf.
Qatar and Abu Dhabi are currently scheduled for **November 29 and December 6**, forming a triple-header with Las Vegas.
It remains **unclear whether F1 will race in the Middle East at all in 2026** if the conflict doesn't ease.

depth.background: F1's 2026 calendar was set to close with a Middle East swing — Qatar and Abu Dhabi in late November and early December — but escalating fighting between Iran, Israel, and the US this year has repeatedly put those races in doubt. F1 had already ruled out a US race as a replacement, and had set a **mid-September deadline** to make a final call, buying time in hopes the conflict would cool down.

thread.previously: F1 had set a mid-September deadline to decide whether the Qatar and Abu Dhabi Grands Prix — the planned season finale — could go ahead given rising Middle East tensions, while already ruling out a US replacement race.
thread.changed: F1 chief Stefano Domenicali has now confirmed a specific fallback: the championship would end in Europe, with Imola tipped as the likely replacement venue, if the Gulf races are scrapped. The update comes right after Tuesday's direct Iranian missile attack on a US base in Jordan sharpened doubts over racing in the region at all this year.

stories.title: Iran strikes Kuwait and Jordan, killing one, hours after the US hit targets inside Iran
stories.what_happened: Early Thursday, July 30, Iran launched missiles and drones at Jordan and Kuwait. Jordanian air defenses intercepted and destroyed **five missiles** headed for the kingdom before they hit anything. In Kuwait, an Iranian strike hit a building belonging to a **Chinese company** in the country's north, killing one worker. Iran said the attacks were retaliation for a fresh round of **US strikes on multiple targets inside Iran**, including Qeshm island, carried out the previous night. The two sides have now traded barrages for five months, with each round of US strikes on Iran answered by an Iranian strike on a US-aligned Gulf state.
key_points: Iran struck **Kuwait and Jordan** with missiles and drones, killing **one worker** at a Chinese-run building in Kuwait's north.
Jordan's air defenses intercepted and shot down **five missiles** early Thursday morning.
The attacks came hours after the **US struck multiple sites inside Iran**, including Qeshm island.
It's the **broadest expansion yet** of the war, after earlier Iranian strikes on Bahrain, Oman and Qatar.
Hopes for a **quick end to the five-month conflict** have dimmed as both sides keep trading strikes.

depth.background: This is part of the wider US-Israel-Iran war that has been running for roughly **five months**, escalating each time Washington or Tehran strikes the other's territory. Iran has increasingly hit back not at Israel or the US directly, but at **Gulf states that host American military bases or are seen as US-aligned** — Kuwait, Jordan, Bahrain, Oman and Qatar have all been targeted this way. Just a day earlier, the war had already spread to Egypt when a drone hit a US-owned gas tanker at the **Damietta port**, showing the conflict's geographic footprint keeps widening.

thread.previously: We reported the Iran war had spread to Egypt when a drone struck a US-owned gas tanker at Damietta port, the first time the conflict hit a country beyond Israel, Iran, and their immediate neighbors.
thread.changed: Iran has now struck two more US-aligned states directly — Kuwait (killing one worker) and Jordan (five missiles shot down) — in retaliation for fresh US strikes inside Iran, marking the most direct expansion of the war into Gulf allies yet.
